rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a material advocacy-letter template for the child. Both letters urge prompt congressional approval of pending legislation, identify an organized public campaign against the proposal, proceed through the opponents' principal claims in a claim-and-rebuttal structure, characterize those objections as false or ill-founded, and close by emphasizing the broader public consequences of rejection. C09 is closely related in subject matter and supplies some of the reorganization-policy rationale, while C11 shares the Hoover Commission, executive-management, efficiency, and urgent-enactment themes, but neither matches the child's extended rebuttal architecture as closely as C13.

shared_material.child_excerpt: However, a public campaign has been instigated against them... The principal objection which has been made to Reorganization Plan No. 1 is... The principal objection which has been made to Plan No. 2 is... The facts refute this claim.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have been shocked in recent days at the extraordinary propaganda campaign that has been unleashed against this bill... The real estate lobby claims... The facts are...
shared_material.explanation: Both frame congressional opposition as an organized publicity campaign and answer its principal claims individually with asserted facts.

shared_material.child_excerpt: These plans propose administrative changes, not changes in legislative policy... Those groups who are opposing these plans on such grounds are creating imaginary difficulties.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The propaganda of the real estate lobby consistently misstates the explicit provisions of the bill, consistently misrepresents what will be the actual effect of the bill, and consistently distorts the facts...
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C13's recurring distinction between what the proposal actually does and the consequences opponents falsely attribute to it.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If plans such as these are rejected, a serious blow will be dealt to the prospects for further progress... I trust, therefore, that the Senate will permit Reorganization Plans No. 1 and No. 2 to become effective.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: But I do not believe the people of our country, nor their representatives in the Congress, will permit themselves to be deceived... I feel confident that the enactment of this legislation will greatly promote the general welfare.
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the rebuttal by warning against obstruction or deception and renewing the request for favorable legislative action.
